title: Addition law for mutually exclusive events
source: S1 Ch4 theory S1-4.2 Quick check 1 (P(A) = 0.42, P(B) = 0.35: 0.77 and 0.23)
stem:
Events \(A\) and \(B\) are mutually exclusive, with \(\mathrm{P}(A)={a|raw}\) and \(\mathrm{P}(B)={b|raw}\).
(a) Find \(\mathrm{P}(A\cup B)\).
(b) Find the probability that neither \(A\) nor \(B\) occurs.

steps.name: U
steps.note: Mutually exclusive, so add: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).

contexts.note: base stem, params and step texts above

contexts.stem:
Each day Mina travels to school in exactly one way. The probability that she walks is {a|raw} and the probability that she takes the bus is {b|raw}.
(a) Find the probability that she walks or takes the bus.
(b) Find the probability that she does neither.

A ball is taken at random from a bag of coloured balls. The probability that it is red is {a|raw} and the probability that it is green is {b|raw}.
(a) Find the probability that the ball is red or green.
(b) Find the probability that the ball is neither red nor green.

title: General addition law: finding P(A and B)
source: S1 Ch4 theory S1-4.2 Quick check 2 (P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, P(A ∪ B) = 0.8: 0.3)
stem: Events \(A\) and \(B\) are such that \(\mathrm{P}(A)={a|raw}\), \(\mathrm{P}(B)={b|raw}\) and \(\mathrm{P}(A\cup B)={u|raw}\). Find \(\mathrm{P}(A\cap B)\).

steps.name: Im
steps.note: Rearrange P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).

contexts.note: base stem, params and step texts above

contexts.stem: In a survey, the proportion of people who own a bicycle is {a|raw}, the proportion who own a car is {b|raw}, and the proportion who own a bicycle or a car or both is {u|raw}. Find the proportion who own both a bicycle and a car.

One student is chosen at random from a school. The probability that the student studies French is {a|raw}, the probability that the student studies Spanish is {b|raw}, and the probability that the student studies French or Spanish or both is {u|raw}. Find the probability that the student studies both languages.

title: Overlapping events: multiples of two numbers
source: S1 Ch4 theory S1-4.2 Quick check 3 (1 to 6, multiple of 2 or 3: 4/6 ≈ 0.667)
stem: A whole number is chosen at random from 1 to {n|int}. Find the probability that it is a multiple of 2 or a multiple of 3.

steps.name: cAB
steps.text_tex: Multiples of both {a|int} and {b|int} are the multiples of {l|int}: \({cAB|int}\)

steps.name: c
steps.note: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B): do not count the overlap twice.

contexts.note: base stem, params and step texts above

contexts.stem: A card is taken at random from {n|int} cards numbered 1 to {n|int}. Find the probability that the number on the card is a multiple of 3 or a multiple of 4.
Raffle tickets are numbered 1 to {n|int}. One ticket is drawn at random. A prize is given if the number is a multiple of 2 or a multiple of 5. Find the probability that the ticket drawn wins a prize.

title: Venn diagram counts: both and exactly one
source: S1 Ch4 theory S1-4.2 Quick check 4 (30 students, choir 12, band 15, neither 7: both 4, P(exactly one) = 19/30)
stem:
In a group of {N|int} students, {c|int} sing in the choir, {d|int} play in the band and {z|int} do neither.
(a) Find the number of students who do both.
(b) One student is chosen at random. Find the probability that the student does exactly one of these activities.

steps.name: Xm
steps.note: n(C) + n(D) counts the overlap twice; total = n(C) + n(D) − n(C ∩ D) + neither.

contexts.note: base stem, params and step texts above

contexts.stem:
In a club of {N|int} members, {c|int} play football, {d|int} play basketball and {z|int} play neither.
(a) Find the number of members who play both.
(b) One member is chosen at random. Find the probability that the member plays exactly one of these sports.

In a survey of {N|int} families, {c|int} have a cat, {d|int} have a dog and {z|int} have neither.
(a) Find the number of families that have both.
(b) One family is chosen at random. Find the probability that the family has exactly one of these pets.

title: Two-way information: either one event or the other or both

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (UCLES). Only part (i) is used; part (ii) is independence (later section).

stem:
In a group of 30 teenagers, 13 of the 18 males watch ‘Kops are Kids’ on television and 3 of the 12
females watch ‘Kops are Kids’.

parts.stem:
Find the probability that a person chosen at random from the group is either female or watches
‘Kops are Kids’ or both.

steps.name: m
steps.text_tex: Females: 12; males who watch: 13. These groups do not overlap.
steps.note: MS: M1 valid attempt to find P(F or W).

steps.name: ex
steps.note: MS: A1 correct unsimplified expression; also accepted: 1 − 5/30, or 12/30 + 16/30 − 3/30.

title: Two groups: either one event or the other or both
source: Similar to 9709/63/O/N/11 Q2(i); authored marks B1 M1 A1 A1 follow that MS
stem: In a group of {N|int} teenagers, {m|int} of the {M|int} males watch a certain television programme and {f|int} of the {F|int} females watch it. Find the probability that a person chosen at random from the group is either female or watches the programme or both.

steps.name: PF
steps.note: Correct probability for one of the groups.

steps.name: cm
steps.text_tex: Females: \({F|int}\); males who watch: \({m|int}\). These groups do not overlap.

steps.name: ex
steps.note: Correct unsimplified expression (or 1 − non-watching males ÷ total).

contexts.stem: A company has {M|int} office staff and {F|int} factory staff. {m|int} of the office staff and {f|int} of the factory staff cycle to work.
